title: Will a price cut raise revenue?

readouts.v: unit elastic: revenue about the same (£19,800: the % rule is approximate for a 10% change)

predict.q: A product sells 1,000 units at £20. The firm cuts the price by 10% to £18. Demand is price elastic, with PED = −2. What happens to total revenue?

options.fb: With PED −2, quantity rises by 20%, twice the 10% price cut: revenue rises from £20,000 to £21,600.
Each unit earns less, but with PED −2 quantity rises 20%, twice the price cut: revenue rises to £21,600.

options.s: It stays the same, because the price cut and the extra sales cancel out
options.fb: They cancel only when PED is about −1. Here quantity rises by 20% and price falls by 10%.

options.s: It cannot change, because only costs change revenue
options.fb: Revenue = price × quantity. Both changed, so revenue changed: to £21,600.

task: Move the **PED** slider from −0.5 to −3 and watch quantity and the revenue rectangle.

target.do: Move the PED slider (try −0.5 to −3), then press Check.

takeaway: A price cut (penetration, competitive pricing) raises revenue only when demand is price elastic.
